summary: Defines a master key used between a PANA client and an enforcement point to bootstrap lower-layer ciphering. It is derived from the EAP Master Session Key after PANA authentication succeeds, and keeps keys independent across enforcement points. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: After you show your ID once, you and the gate guard get a private key to lock your chats, and each guard gets a different one.

questions: derive key from eap msk for pana
how is the pemk derived from the msk
what is a pana enforcement point
subtitle: How a PANA client and a network gatekeeper get a shared key, derived from the EAP session key, that no other gatekeeper shares.

tldr.problem: After a client authenticates to a network with PANA, the enforcement point that filters its traffic needs a shared secret to turn on encryption, and each enforcement point needs a different one.
tldr.mechanism: A 64-octet PaC-EP Master Key (PEMK) is derived from the EAP Master Session Key with prf+, mixing in the session identifier, the key identifier and the enforcement point's identifier.
tldr.outcome: Each client and enforcement point pair gets its own key, whose lifetime cannot outlast the MSK. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted.

today: RFC 5807 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2010. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 5807 builds on the Protocol for carrying Authentication for Network Access (PANA, RFC 5191). PANA carries the Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP, RFC 3748) between a PANA Client (PaC) and a PANA Authentication Agent (PAA). The PAA acts as a gateway to the Authentication Server (AS).

This document defines one thing: the PaC-EP Master Key (PEMK). A secure association protocol uses it as the pre-shared secret between the PaC and an Enforcement Point (EP) so that cryptographic filters can be enabled in the access network. The RFC also gives a guideline for getting PEMKs from the PAA to the EP.

It does not say how a PaC learns whether the lower layer needs a secure association protocol or a secret bootstrapped from PANA. Each lower-layer protocol may define that.
sections.eli5: Once the network has checked who you are, this document says how you and the guard at the door can share a secret code. How you find out you need the code is left to someone else.

sections.title: The Players and Where the Key Fits
sections.content:
The PANA framework (RFC 5193) adds an Enforcement Point (EP) to the picture. The EP sits in the access network. It lets data traffic from authorized clients through and blocks everyone else, depending on the PANA authentication and authorization result. The EP and the PAA may run on the same device or on separate ones.

The EP can use non-cryptographic or cryptographic filters, applied at the link layer or the IP layer. With cryptographic filtering, a secure association protocol (for example IKE or a 4-way handshake) runs between the PaC and the EP. When it finishes, link- or network-layer per-packet security such as IPsec ESP is enabled. That gives integrity protection, data origin authentication, replay protection and, optionally, confidentiality.

The secure association protocol needs a pre-shared secret to start from. The PEMK is that secret.
sections.eli5: The guard at the door only lets people in who passed the ID check. To talk privately with each visitor, the guard and the visitor need a secret code first, and the PEMK is that code.

sections.title: Deriving the PEMK
sections.content:
A PEMK is derived from an available Master Session Key (MSK). It is 64 octets long and is computed as PEMK = prf+(MSK, "IETF PEMK" | SID | KID | EPID), where | means concatenation.

  • prf+ is the function defined in IKEv2 (RFC 4306). The underlying pseudo-random function is the one named in the PRF-Algorithm AVP of the PANA-Auth-Request message that has the 'S' (Start) bit set.
  • "IETF PEMK" is the ASCII string without the quotes and without a NULL terminator.
  • SID is the four-octet PANA Session Identifier.
  • KID is the content of the Key-ID AVP associated with the MSK.
  • EPID is the identifier of the EP. Its first two octets are the AddressType, an Address Family from the IANA registry, and the remaining octets encode the address. The AddressType decides the length and format of the address value.

Because the EPID combines an address family with an address, PEMKs for different EPs are cryptographically independent, even across address families. How a PaC discovers an EPID is out of scope.
sections.eli5: You take one master secret and stir in a few labels, like the session number and the guard's name tag. Change the name tag and you get a completely different key.

sections.title: Key Name, Scope, Context and Lifetime
sections.content:
The key name is PEMKname = SHA1(EPID | SID | KID), using SHA-1 from the Secure Hash Standard. Including the EPID, SID and KID makes names unique across the PaC-EP pairs under a given PAA.

Scope: one PEMK is used between one PaC and one EP, and it MUST NOT be shared among multiple PaCs or EPs.

Context: a PEMK is the pre-shared key of the secure association protocol within its scope, and it MUST NOT be used for any other purpose.

Lifetime: a PEMK's lifetime MUST be less than or equal to that of the MSK it came from. At the end of its lifetime, the PEMK and its associated state MUST be deleted.
sections.eli5: Each key has a label, belongs to just one visitor and one guard, is used only for their private chat, and must be thrown away when the original ticket runs out.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC follows the AAA key management guidance in RFC 4962. Key lifetime, scope, context and name are covered by the rules above.

Channel binding. Since the EP's identifier goes into the key derivation, the PEMK is bound between the PaC and the PAA when it is generated. If a malicious EP advertises a device identifier different from the one registered with the PAA, the PaC and the EP compute different PEMKs and the secure association protocol fails.

Distributing the PEMK. If the EP runs on the same device as the PAA, no protocol is needed. If it runs on a separate device, a key distribution protocol is needed. It MUST ensure the PEMK is encrypted, integrity protected and replay protected, using a security association between the PAA and EP. That security association MUST be cryptographically bound to the identities of the PAA and EP known to the PaC.
sections.eli5: If a fake guard claims to be someone else, its secret code will not match yours, so the private chat never starts. When the code travels between offices, it must go in a locked, sealed box.

items.title: MSK
items.text: The EAP Master Session Key the PEMK is derived from.

items.title: KID
items.text: Content of the Key-ID AVP tied to the MSK.

items.title: EPID
items.text: Two-octet AddressType followed by the EP's address.
